note: Product-intent confirmation record. The brief (2026-11-17): 'For each submitted link, store the intended ASIN, official listing URL, confirmation date, and source. Keep observed redirect targets in a separate field. Do not merge the two fields.' The intended half is what the OWNER says a submitted link was minted for; it may only be filled from a stated source (the owner's confirmation inside Associates Central, or a written instruction). The observed half is what this project MEASURED when it opened the link. Nothing in the observed half is ever copied into the intended half: where a link happens to go is evidence about the link, not a claim about intent. Rationale (brief): Amazon's ASIN definition provides a checkable identifier — a 10-character code that addresses exactly one catalog record — so an intended ASIN is a falsifiable claim, while a 9-character short-link code is not.

schema.intended.asin: 10-character ASIN the owner confirms this link was minted for. BLANK until the owner states it — never inferred from observed.asin.
schema.intended.official_listing_url: canonical listing URL for that ASIN. BLANK until intended.asin is filled from a stated source.
schema.intended.confirmation_date: date the owner confirmed. BLANK until then.
schema.intended.confirmation_source: where the confirmation came from (e.g. 'Associates Central link checker, read by owner, <date>'). BLANK until then.
schema.observed.redirect_targets: dated list of where the link actually went when this project opened it. Volatile per-arrival parameters (btn_ref shuffle tokens) are noted, not stored as identity.
schema.observed.asin: ASIN parsed from the observed destination URL. Observation only.
schema.observed.listing_title: title the destination page served on the observation date. Perishable evidence — the date is part of the value.
